title: Indian Court Allows Exceptional Liver Transplant for Minor
summary: A 17-year-old Indian boy has been granted permission by the Delhi High Court to donate part of his liver to his ailing father, who requires a transplant. The court's decision is seen as an exceptional case, allowing for the first time in India such a liver donation between family members. This move highlights the complexities and nuances of organ transplantation laws in India.
summary_points: A 17-year-old Indian boy has been granted permission by the Delhi High Court to donate part of his liver to his father.
This is an exceptional case, allowing for the first time in India such a liver donation between family members.
The court's decision highlights the complexities and nuances of organ transplantation laws in India.
Organ transplantation laws in India are often criticized for being restrictive and not keeping pace with international standards.
The government has been under pressure to relax these laws, allowing more flexibility for organ donations.
